new_scholarship.description: The K.C. Kuok Scholarship is a Monash University award funded and named after Monash alumnus Khoon Chen Kuok (Beau Kuok) that supports financially disadvantaged international students to complete a full-time undergraduate degree at a Monash University campus in Australia. One scholarship is available in 2026 for commencement in February 2027, and the official page states a total scholarship value of up to AUD $360,000 over four years. Applicants must be citizens of mainland China, Indonesia, Hong Kong or a Southeast Asian country, must not have commenced university study at any institution, and must demonstrate that they come from a low income household. Selection is based on outstanding academic achievement and financial disadvantage, assessed through a personal aspiration statement, a financial support statement and interview performance.
new_scholarship.best_fit: An international student who is a citizen of mainland China, Indonesia, Hong Kong or a Southeast Asian country, has never commenced university study at any institution and has not previously studied at Monash, is applying for a full-time single (non-double) undergraduate degree at a Monash Australian campus, can demonstrate with certified and English-translated documents that they come from a low income household, has strong academic results, and can write a 400-500 word personal aspiration statement and a 400-500 word financial support statement and perform well in an English-language online interview.
new_scholarship.funding_period: over four years (total package value, published by Monash as 'up to')
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be an international student and a citizen of mainland China, Indonesia, Hong Kong or a Southeast Asian country (Monash links the term 'Southeast Asian country' to the Australian Government DFAT Southeast Asia page). They must apply for a full-time Monash course offer in any single degree at a Monash University campus in Australia; double degree applicants are not eligible. They must have not previously studied at Monash, must not have commenced university study at any institution, and must demonstrate that they come from a low income household, evidenced by certified documents of the family's tax forms. Applicants must achieve the minimum entry requirements for their preferred Monash course, including English language requirements. Selection is based on outstanding academic achievement and financial disadvantage, assessed on the personal aspiration statement, the financial support statement and interview performance. One scholarship is available in 2026 for February 2027 commencement; the panel may award additional scholarships where there is more than one outstanding applicant. To retain the scholarship recipients must maintain a minimum Weighted Average Mark of 50 and a full-time study load, and the scholarship cannot be deferred.

new_scholarship.english_requirement: IELTS (Academic) 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0, or TOEFL iBT 79 overall, or Pearson Test of English (Academic) 58 with no communicative skills score below 50. These are Monash's published minimum undergraduate English language requirements; some courses set higher requirements, and international students must also meet the Department of Home Affairs English language visa requirements, which differ from Monash's. English test results must have been achieved within three years before the course commencement date. The scholarship's own applicant information pack states that applicants forward high school results (and HKDSE English results for Hong Kong applicants) as the evidence for the English requirement, and the interview is conducted in English.
new_scholarship.selection_notes: Selection is by a Monash University panel. The official page states the scholarship 'will be awarded based on outstanding academic achievement and financial disadvantage' and that 'Students will be assessed on their personal aspiration statement and financial support statement and interview performance.' The application form adds that the panel also takes into account academic achievements, extra-curricular activities and community involvements, and lists academic results as a fourth assessment input. No numeric weighting between academic achievement, financial disadvantage, the two statements and the interview is published. Shortlisting ran in the weeks beginning 21 July to 7 August 2026; shortlisted candidates were advised in the week beginning 10 August 2026; final round online interviews were held on 15 August 2026; and all applicants were advised of the outcome by the week beginning 17 August 2026. One scholarship is available in 2026, and the panel may elect to award additional scholarships where there is more than one outstanding applicant.
new_scholarship.notes: All facts come from official monash.edu content. Two official Monash documents linked from the scholarship page (the applicant information pack and the offline application form) are hosted on Google Drive with owner-disabled download, so their contents were read by rendering the PDF viewer in a browser; both remain official Monash documents linked from the official page. The 'Southeast Asian country' criterion is defined by Monash only by reference to the Australian Government DFAT Southeast Asia page, which could not be read on the verification date because it redirects to an unrelated DFAT page; no country list has therefore been asserted. The official web page lists 'Student visa costs' while the applicant information pack explicitly lists international student health insurance as covered; insurance is recorded from the pack and flagged as lower confidence. There is an internal inconsistency across official documents on the academic retention threshold: one FAQ answer in the applicant information pack states a minimum WAM of 65, while two other answers in the same pack and the official web page state WAM 50; WAM 50 is recorded because it is the figure on the official scholarship page. Monash publishes no per-course tuition value, so the 'up to AUD $360,000' total is recorded exactly as published and was not recomputed.

programme_detail_official.tuition_coverage_note: Monash states that 'your tuition fee and related study costs (accommodation, airfares and more) will be fully supported'. The official benefit list states 'Tuition fees' and the applicant information pack states 'Full tuition fees paid for duration of course'. Monash publishes no per-course or per-year tuition figure, so the tuition component cannot be quantified from official sources and the published total of 'up to $360,000 AUD over four years' is recorded as published rather than recomputed. programme_detail_official.english_requirement_note: The scholarship page itself publishes no English test scores. The scores recorded are Monash University's published minimum undergraduate English language requirements from the official Monash admissions English language requirements page: IELTS (Academic) and its UKVI, One Skill Retake and Online variants 6.5 overall with Reading, Listening, Writing and Speaking 6.0; TOEFL iBT 79 overall (0-20 scale) with Reading 13, Listening 12, Writing 21, Speaking 18; TOEFL iBT 4 overall (1-6 scale); TOEFL Essentials 8; Pearson Test of English (Academic) and PTE (Academic) UKVI 58 with no communicative skills score below 50; Cambridge C1 Advanced and C2 Proficiency 176 with 169 in each skill; LanguageCert Academic 67. Duolingo is not listed in Monash's published minimum English test score table. Some courses set higher requirements than the university minimum. Applicants who completed six years of schooling at an English medium institution in an English-speaking country before age 19 may meet the requirement through schooling or prior tertiary study rather than a test. International students must also meet the Department of Home Affairs English language visa requirements, which differ from Monash's. The scholarship's own applicant information pack states that applicants forward high school results (and HKDSE English results for Hong Kong applicants) as the evidence for the English requirement.

programme_detail_official.description: The K.C. Kuok Scholarship is a Monash University award funded and named after Monash alumnus Khoon Chen Kuok, better known as Beau Kuok, that supports financially disadvantaged international students from mainland China, Indonesia, Hong Kong and Southeast Asia to complete a full-time undergraduate degree at any of Monash's Australian campuses. One scholarship is available in 2026 for commencement in February 2027, with a total value stated by Monash as up to AUD $360,000 over four years. The package covers tuition fees, an allowance of AUD $14,000 per year, accommodation at Monash University Accommodation, student visa costs, a one-off establishment payment of AUD $3,000 in the first year and the first incoming flight to Australia. Selection is based on outstanding academic achievement and financial disadvantage, assessed through a personal aspiration statement, a financial support statement and interview performance, and recipients must maintain a minimum Weighted Average Mark of 50 and a full-time study load to retain the award.
programme_detail_official.program_type: University donor-funded equity scholarship (institutional, competitive, separate application)
programme_detail_official.coverage: Full tuition fees for the duration of the course (maximum four years), a living allowance of AUD $14,000 per full year, on-campus accommodation at Monash University Accommodation for standard academic-calendar contract periods, student visa (subclass 500) costs, international student health insurance, a one-off establishment payment of AUD $3,000 in the first year, and the first incoming flight to Australia. Excluded: summer accommodation fees, flights in years 2-4 (funded from the recipient's allowance), international study exchange costs, and any travel or accommodation for accompanying family. The published total of 'up to $360,000 AUD over four years' is Monash's upper estimate for the package, not a guaranteed sum, and Monash publishes no per-course tuition figure from which it can be independently reconstructed.

research_notes.degree_level_confirmed: Confirmed from the official Monash scholarship page, which opens 'Are you an international student looking to enrol in an undergraduate degree?' and requires applicants to 'Apply for a full-time Monash course offer in any single degree, at Monash University, at a campus in Australia'. The official applicant information pack states the scholarship 'will cover costs for any undergraduate degree' and is 'for commencement in February, 2027', and the application form asks for 'Intake: Semester 1, 2027'. The award funds a full bachelor's degree and its support is capped at four years, which matches a bachelor's degree. No master's or doctoral funding is described.
research_notes.assignment_note: This target is listed in the Rejected section of ASSIGNMENTS.md with the reason 'registrable domain already in DB: LIVE/id52/Monash International Leadership Scholarship'. That rejection reflects the batch's in-batch host-uniqueness filter, not an actual duplicate award. On checking the live database, programme_details.json contains no K.C. Kuok Scholarship record, and the only Monash-hosted record (id 52) is a materially different award: the Monash International Leadership Scholarship is open to international students from all countries, pays 100% of course fees only and explicitly excludes OSHC, accommodation and living costs, is awarded automatically on receipt of an unconditional offer with no application, and is offered four times per year. The K.C. Kuok Scholarship is restricted to citizens of mainland China, Indonesia, Hong Kong and Southeast Asia, covers tuition plus a living allowance, accommodation, visa costs, health insurance, an establishment payment and the first flight, requires a separate scholarship application and an interview, and is offered once per cycle. It is therefore neither in the database nor a near-duplicate, so per RESEARCH_PROTOCOL.md section 5 the target was not excluded and no substitution was made.
